comments.value:
Hello, thanks for your report.
Would you be able to provide us with more information on this issue? In particular, the repro steps you have provided are far too generic, and cannot be used to reproduce the issue.
We are interested in these bits of info:
- Step-by-step, specific instructions to reproduce the problem
- Output logs
- Crash dumps
- Screenshots
- Video
- Any other relevant information
Treat the issue as if you're trying to show us how to make it happen. If we can cause the bug to occur, on our end, it makes it a ton easier to fix. If that isn't possible, documenting what it looks like when the bug happens might help.
FYI: Your output logs are stored in `C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\LocalLow\VRChat\vrchat`. They're text files, and they're named `output_log_HH-MM-SS.txt`. The time stamp shows the time at which that log started, so make sure you give us the right one.
It's a hidden folder, so you might have some problems tracking it down. Try pasting this into your File Browser address bar: `%AppData\..\LocalLow\VRChat\vrchat`.
You can paste the contents of that file into [pastebin](https://pastebin.com), [gist](https://gist.github.com/), [0bin](https://0bin.net/), or a similar service.
For this particular issue, it may also be useful to track down crash dumps. These are lower-level crash logs that will require some more work to debug, but you should probably find them and let us know if you have them. 
If you have them, they will be in this folder:
`%UserProfile%\AppData\Local\CrashDumps`
If you have any Dump Files in this folder that say "VRChat.exe" at the beginning of the filename, you've found them.

details:
I could never actually find out why before, as nothing ever showed up upon crashing, it just closed, but this time for some reason it showed a window that let me open visual studio for debugging and the cause appears to be an access violation in unityplayer.dll.

My hard drive is not full.
My memory is not being maxed out (I have 24gb).
It happens in both vr and desktop (ruling out steamvr as the cause as someone else had suggested).
It specifically appears to happen when any event in game is triggered. A current list of things that have had my game crash right after are:
Playing an animation
Opening the menu
When the menu loads more items
Changing avatars (myself or anyone else)
title: Game randomly freezes and/or crashes due to access violation.
